document.headline: Inventory 3.0 was conceived and created today.

subject.mainFocus: Creating Inventory 3.0 as a new personal inventory system while unifying the Klinswork tools, correcting mobile behavior, and establishing more reliable image and branding workflows.
subject.description: Klinswork work update for July 21, 2026, covering Inventory 3.0, Tool Center improvements, mobile fixes, image troubleshooting, and next steps.

narrative.promptingSituation: Earlier inventory versions had become patchwork, while the growing Klinswork tool set still behaved like separate experiments. Mobile scaling, cropped images, inconsistent icons, and product-image problems also limited practical use.
narrative.initialUnderstanding: A new inventory system should begin as a fresh architecture rather than another repair, and the surrounding tool environment needed coordinated mobile, branding, and image improvements.
narrative.intendedOutcome: Create a stable personal inventory foundation, make the Tool Center a coherent entrance to the applications, and correct the most important mobile and visual problems.
narrative.approach: Separate configuration, data access, business rules, and validation into focused backend files; refine the Tool Center; diagnose viewport and image behavior; repair branding assets; and document a future batch-image workflow.

progression.title: Defined Inventory 3.0 as a fresh system
progression.description: Rejected another patch to prior inventory versions and established a new architecture.
progression.result: Four focused backend service files and a clear personal inventory purpose were established.

progression.title: Unified the Klinswork entry point
progression.description: Refined the Tool Center to present Inventory 3.0, Tasker, and Email Composer as one system.
progression.result: The tools gained a common entrance, clearer identity, and improved mobile access.

progression.title: Diagnosed mobile and image failures
progression.description: Corrected missing viewport metadata and replaced cropping behavior with proportional responsive image rules.
progression.result: Pages rendered at readable mobile scale and complete images remained visible.

progression.title: Resolved branding and product-image issues
progression.description: Worked through favicon formats, home-screen icons, manifests, transparency, halos, and product-image artifacts.
progression.result: Branding behavior was clarified and product imagery was repaired for practical interface use.

problemsEncountered.problem: The Apps Script page appeared as a tiny desktop page on a phone.
problemsEncountered.effect: Text and cards were difficult to use on mobile.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Added the viewport meta tag through doGet() and redeployed.

problemsEncountered.problem: Images became cropped after mobile scaling was corrected.
problemsEncountered.effect: Important portions of product and interface images were cut away.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Removed fixed-height cropping behavior and used height:auto with object-fit:contain.

problemsEncountered.problem: Favicon and home-screen icon behavior was inconsistent.
problemsEncountered.effect: Branding updates did not appear reliably across browsers and phones.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Separated favicon, manifest, and home-screen icon responsibilities, corrected formats and dimensions, redeployed, and accounted for caching.

problemsEncountered.problem: The Prominence product image contained a gray background and right-edge artifact.
problemsEncountered.effect: The image looked poor inside Inventory 3.0.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Recreated the edge and produced both clean and white-background versions.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Continuing to patch earlier inventory versions.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItWasTried: It would have reused existing work.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: The update explicitly concluded that Inventory 3.0 needed a fresh start and stable architecture.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: A clean boundary is preferable when accumulated patches obscure responsibilities.

unsuccessfulApproaches.approach: Using fixed image heights with object-fit:cover.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whyItDidNotWork: It cropped image content after the mobile layout was corrected.
unsuccessfulApproaches.whatWasLearned: Product and documentation images should preserve their full proportions.

turningPoints.title: Inventory 3.0 became a new system rather than an update
turningPoints.description: The work explicitly reframed the inventory effort as a clean architecture.
turningPoints.effectOnDirection: Development moved toward separated services and a durable personal system.

turningPoints.title: Viewport repair exposed the image problem

turningPoints.effectOnDirection: Responsive image rules were revised rather than treating the viewport fix as complete.

keyDecisions.decision: Separate configuration, data access, business logic, and validation.
keyDecisions.reason: The new system should avoid becoming one large script file.
alternativesConsidered: Place all logic in a single script
consequences: Future testing and maintenance became easier.

keyDecisions.decision: Use the Tool Center as the common entrance to the apps.
keyDecisions.reason: The applications should operate as one coherent personal system instead of isolated experiments.
alternativesConsidered: Keep separate entry points without shared presentation
consequences: Shared branding and navigation became more important.
Inventory 3.0, Tasker, and Email Composer gained a visible relationship.

keyDecisions.decision: Preserve complete images rather than crop them into fixed boxes.
keyDecisions.reason: Product and documentation images need to remain fully legible.
consequences: Card layouts may need to accommodate natural image height.

narrative.methodEstablished: Treat mobile layout, responsive images, browser favicons, mobile home-screen icons, manifests, and image transparency as separate technical concerns and test each one directly.
narrative.result: Inventory 3.0 was established as a new structured application, while the broader Klinswork environment became more unified, mobile-friendly, recognizable, and practical.
lessonsLearned: A viewport fix can reveal separate responsive-image problems.
Browser favicons and mobile home-screen icons are different delivery mechanisms.
Checkerboard appearance must be tested to determine whether transparency is real or baked into the image.
Repeated manual image cleanup justifies an automated batch-processing workflow.

sections.title: Issues diagnosed and troubleshooting fixes
sections.contentSummary: Phone layout appeared tiny The Apps Script page was initially being rendered at desktop width and then shrunk to fit the phone. The cause was a missing viewport setting in doGet() . After saving and redeploying, the page rendered at the correct mobile scale. Text became readable, cards became usable, and the interface stopped behaving like a miniature desktop page. Images cropped after the mobile fix Once the page scaled correctly, some images were cropped because fixed heights and object-fit: cover were forcing them to fill boxes by cutting away part of the image. The corrected approach preserves the complete image, maintains its proportions, and allows it to flex naturally with the page. sections.title: Image preparation and transparency work
sections.contentSummary: Product and interface images were reviewed and adjusted so they work more reliably inside Inventory 3.0 and the Tool Center. Topics worked through Exact pixel dimensions PNG versus JPEG White and transparent backgrounds Alpha channels Checkerboard transparency Flattening and merged layers Gray halos and edge artifacts Scaling without cropping Reliable transparency test Place a bright-colored layer underneath the image in GIMP: If the color shows through, the pixels are transparent. If the checkerboard remains, it is baked into the image. Prominence product-image repair The Prominence floor-cleaner image had a gray background and a strange vertical artifact on the right. The product image was recreated with a clean edge, and a second version was produced with a solid white background for simple use in the inventory interface. sections.title: The larger achievement
sections.contentSummary: Today combined creation and troubleshooting. Inventory 3.0 was conceived and created, while the surrounding Klinswork environment became more unified, mobile-friendly, recognizable, and practical. A new inventory architecture was established. The Tool Center became the common entrance to the work apps. Mobile scaling was corrected. Responsive image behavior was improved. Browser branding and mobile installation requirements were clarified. Product images were repaired and standardized. A future image-automation workflow was identified. By the end of the day, the separate projects were becoming a coherent personal work-software system with one entrance, consistent branding, mobile access, structured inventory services, communication tools, and a foundation for continued automation.

email.subject: Inventory 3.0 and Klinswork Tool Center Update
email.body: Inventory 3.0 was started as a new personal inventory system with a cleaner modular foundation. The Klinswork Tool Center was also improved so the main work tools are presented together, and several mobile, image, and branding problems were corrected. The inventory application remains in early development, with continued implementation and image standardization as the next steps.
